==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|flām}}, {{IPA|en|/fleɪm/}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-flame.wav|a=GA}} * {{audio|en|en-us-flame.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪm|s=1}} * {{homophones|en|Flaim}} ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|id=fire|:inh|enm:flawme}} From {{inh|en|enm|flawme}}, blend of {{der|en|fro|flame}} and {{m|fro|flambe}}, {{m|fro|flamble}}, the first from {{der|en|la|flamma}}, the second from {{der|en|la|flammula|}}, diminutive of {{m|la|flamma}}, both from pre-Latin *''fladma''; {{der|en|itc-pro|*flagmā}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰel-||to shimmer, gleam, shine}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|līeġ}}. ====Noun==== [[Image:Flame.JPG|right|thumb|100px]] {{en-noun|~}} # {{senseid|en|Q235544}}The visible part of [[fire]]; a [[stream]] of [[burning]] [[vapor|vapour]] or [[gas]], emitting [[light]] and [[heat]]. #* {{RQ:Chambers Younger Set|III|passage=Long after his cigar burnt bitter, he sat with eyes fixed on the blaze. When the '''flames''' at last began to flicker and subside, his lids fluttered, then drooped; but he had lost all reckoning of time when he opened them again to find Miss Erroll in furs and ball-gown kneeling on the hearth{{nb...}}.}} #* {{RQ:Guardian|date=2012-08-21|title=Paralympic flames light up countdown to biggest Games in history|author=Alexandra Topping|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2012/aug/21/paralympic-flames-countdown-biggest-games |passage=The '''flames''' will then be joined together next week at Stoke Mandeville in Buckinghamshire, the home of the Paralympics, and the united '''flame''' will make its final journey to London for the opening of the 14th Paralympic Games next Wednesday.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=July-August|author=w:Henry Petroski |url=http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/2013/4/geothermal-energy|title=Geothermal Energy |volume=101|issue=4|magazine=w:American Scientist |passage=Energy has seldom been found where we need it when we want it. Ancient nomads, wishing to ward off the evening chill and enjoy a meal around a campfire, had to collect wood and then spend time and effort coaxing the heat of friction out from between sticks to kindle a '''flame'''.}} # A [[romantic]] [[partner]] or [[lover]] in a usually short-lived but [[passionate]] [[affair]]. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:lover}} #* {{RQ:Thackeray Barry Lyndon|chapter=XIX|passage=I could copy out yards of rhapsody to Lord George Poynings, her old '''flame''', in which she addressed him by the most affectionate names.}} # {{lb|en|Internet|somewhat|dated}} An aggressively insulting criticism or remark. # A brilliant reddish orange-gold fiery colour. {{color panel|FF4D00}} # {{lb|en|music|chiefly|lutherie}} The contrasting light and dark figure seen in wood used for stringed instrument making; the [[curl]]. #: {{ux|en|The cello has a two-piece back with a beautiful narrow '''flame'''.}} # Burning [[zeal]], [[passion]], [[imagination]], [[excitement]], or [[anger]]. #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=5|passage=in a '''flame''' of zeal severe|year=1873}} #* {{RQ:Pope Works|title=Eloisa to Abelard|passage=where '''flames''' refin'd in breasts seraphic glow}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1834|author=w:Samuel Taylor Coleridge|title=Julia |passage=Till charming Florio, born to conquer, came
And touch'd the fair one with an equal '''flame'''}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|botany}} A [[variety]] of [[carnation]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1718|author={{w|Richard Bradley (botanist)|Richard Bradley}}|chapter=Part II. Chapter II: ''Of'' Perannual Flowers, ''the talleſt Blowers''. Sect IX. ''Of the'' Carnation ''or'' July-Flower {{...}}|title=New Improvements of Planting and Gardening, Both Philoſophical and Practical {{...}}|edition=2nd|location=London|publisher=W.
